jobs.title: Director of Product Management (EF0E85E)
jobs.description:
Referment is working with a workplace financial wellbeing business that combines digital planning tools with professional guidance. Its products help employees make decisions about their money, while giving employers a financial wellbeing benefit for workforces across different countries and financial systems.

As Director of Product Management, you'll set product strategy across the employee experience and the platform capabilities behind it. The remit combines organisational leadership with hands-on work: you'll develop Product Managers and Designers while working closely with Engineering to shape solutions, make tradeoffs and carry priorities through discovery and delivery.

Reporting to the COO, you'll connect member needs, enterprise client requirements and commercial opportunities into a clear direction. A central part of the work is deciding how to measure meaningful financial outcomes, rather than treating engagement alone as success. You'll also assess where AI can improve the product and how it can support research, prototyping and the team's day-to-day practice.

The Role

Set and evolve the product vision, strategy and roadmap, translating research and market insight into priorities and measurable outcomes.
Guide both customer-facing experiences and enabling platform investments, accounting for localisation, privacy, regulation and regional differences.
Work directly with Product, Design and Engineering on solution design, scope and delivery decisions.
Build alignment with commercial and operational teams so customer needs and business opportunities inform product choices.
Develop the Product and Design organisation, strengthening its craft, operating model and ways of working.
Identify useful AI applications in financial guidance and build AI-assisted discovery and product-development capabilities across the team.

What We're Looking For

At least 10 years in product management, including ownership of product strategy and experience building or evolving a product organisation.
Proven leadership of Product Managers and Designers, alongside a willingness to stay involved in detailed product decisions.
A track record of improving engagement, retention, customer behaviour or other measurable product outcomes.
Experience spanning customer-facing products and their underlying platforms, with enterprise B2B exposure.
Experience serving global or complex customer environments and making decisions shaped by localisation and regulation.
Clear cross-functional communication and sound judgment when opportunities are ambiguous.

Useful Additional Experience

Benefits, fintech or HR technology experience would be valuable. Regulated financial services, developing a Design practice, AI-powered products and scaling a Product organisation are also relevant backgrounds.

This could suit a product director or hands-on product leader who enjoys developing a team while remaining close to the decisions that shape the customer experience.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Check

Payroll is broken. It's still running on decades-old infrastructure. We're rebuilding it.

We don't run payroll ourselves — we power the businesses that do. As the inventors of embedded payroll, we're redefining how people get paid and making it easier for those businesses to launch, grow, and thrive.

On our team, you'll use creative problem-solving, critical thinking, and grit to simplify the complexity of payroll for thousands of employers of every size, across all industries. We ignore conventional role boundaries in favor of the unique strengths and values each builder brings to our mission: make paying people simple
. Check out our origin story!

Check is far more than just API infrastructure. We’re a springboard for building and scaling payroll businesses. See how it works for our partners.

The Work

We're looking for a Product Manager to own Payouts — how employees and contractors actually get paid across Check's infrastructure. It's a well-scoped, high-trust domain: ACH is live and stable today, and we're gearing up for bigger swings next year. You'll partner closely with a dedicated engineering counterpart, Check leadership, and our partners — software companies across diverse verticals — to keep payouts rock-solid while building what's next.

In This Role, You Will

Own execution on Payouts end-to-end, from ACH today toward same-day pay and new payment methods
Take a well-scoped problem and run with it — you'll be trusted to execute thoroughly and with strong judgment, not just to check boxes
Sweat the details: catch edge cases before they ship and hold a high bar for quality, with minimal need for rework
Know when to make the call yourself and when to loop in your manager — escalation judgment matters as much as independent execution
Partner closely with your dedicated engineering counterpart and cross-functional teams (engineering, operations, partners) to ship reliably
Connect directly with Check's partners to understand how payouts show up in their day-to-day, and translate that into product decisions

Many backgrounds could fit this role, but ideal candidates will have some or all of the following:

Product management experience in technology companies
A track record of thorough, low-iteration execution on well-scoped work — you ship things that don't come back for rework
Good judgment about when to escalate versus handle something yourself
Payments experience is a plus, but not required — payroll and tax knowledge isn't required either; we consider it learnable
Comfort partnering closely with engineering, operations, and external partners to drive a project to completion
Willingness to attend our annual 3-day company offsite in the spring

Travel & Office Policy

The Check team is distributed across the US. Roles can be remote, hybrid, or based in one of our offices in New York City
or San Francisco
. We offer ample opportunities and encourage employees to attend team offsites, events, and hackathons throughout year. All Checketeers gather in the spring for our annual 3-day company retreat.

For our in-office and hybrid employees, our offices are open all week. We provide meals on Tuesdays
and Thursdays
and there are regular happy hours, game nights, and other in-person events.

Remote work at Check requires the ability to perform all responsibilities without distraction or disruption, while maintaining quality, effective communication, and productivity.

Ethos offers instant, accessible products and a seamless online process that requires no medical exams and just a few health questions; it eliminates traditional barriers, making it easier than ever for everyone to protect their families. This team is responsible for building a delightful digital consumer experience — from onboarding users and helping them understand their families' needs, to purchasing the right insurance products to protect what matters most. Communicate product strategy, progress, and results clearly to executive leadership and the broader organization
Drive alignment on shared goals across product, engineering, and business teams to ensure cohesive execution

12+ years of experience as a product manager at a high-growth technology company, building consumer products at significant scale
5+ years of experience managing and developing product managers, with a track record of growing high-performing PM teams
Experience in fintech, insurtech, or other regulated consumer industries is a plus
Exceptional ability to generate, test, and refine hypotheses using a blend of data, user insights, and market trends — ensuring product decisions are both innovative and impactful
Strong analytical orientation with a focus on data-driven decision making; ability to measure success rigorously across a portfolio of bets

At In Tandem, we build technology that helps families manage everyday routines and navigate life's biggest transitions. Through our four brands—OurFamilyWizard, Cozi, FamilyWall, and Custody Navigator—we help families stay organized, communicate well, and foster healthy childhoods.

We believe technology should strengthen relationships and make daily coordination less complicated. Everything we create is designed to lighten the mental load, reduce conflict, and support families through big and small moments.

Enterprise email doesn’t get bought the way consumer email gets downloaded. Someone has to believe Mail will change how their team works, make that case to their own leadership, and then get a few hundred people to actually change a habit they’ve had for a decade. That is the job.

Superhuman Mail is the fastest email experience in the world, and it is loved — see what our customers say. Individuals adopt it in minutes. Organizations are harder: the buyer needs proof, the champion needs ammunition, and the team needs a switch that doesn’t cost them a week of feeling slow.

We’re hiring a Product Manager, Admin & Buyer Experience
to own that arc for Mail — from the moment a buyer starts evaluating us through the moment their team is fully switched over. You’ll own Mail’s admin and usage-visibility surfaces, and you’ll own the onboarding experience that determines whether a signed deal becomes a deployed one.

You’ll spend real time with economic buyers, IT admins, and internal champions, and you’ll work closely with Sales and CS — while holding a clear point of view about which enterprise needs are patterns worth building for and which are one-offs. This is a chance to shape how the world's largest enterprises process their most critical documents in the era of agentic AI.

Own the investment strategy, product vision, roadmap, and end-to-end delivery for the Intelligent Document Processing pillar and the TotalAgility platform — accountable for both the strategic direction and the operational and financial results of the business.

Key Responsibilities

Drive execution end to end. Translate the roadmap into prioritized, well-scoped releases and partner closely with Engineering to ship on schedule, at quality, and with measurable customer impact. This role is accountable for delivery, not just direction.
Own the numbers. Set and own product growth targets in partnership with Finance; be accountable for bookings, revenue growth, net revenue retention (NRR), and gross revenue retention (GRR) in the IDP pillar.
Lead the AI agenda. Own the AI and document-intelligence strategy for the platform — capture, classification, extraction, and agentic document workflows — including build-versus-partner decisions and how AI capabilities are packaged, metered, and priced.
Be the visible face of the product. Stay personally and consistently close to customers and the market — this is a flagship product, and the strategy behind it needs to be shaped in the room with customers, not developed in isolation and handed down. Participate directly in customer meetings, executive briefings, and prospect conversations, and treat that engagement as core to the job, not an occasional add-on.
Own the platform story across the broader portfolio. Drive product strategy and thought leadership not just for TotalAgility, but across the wider DWA portfolio — defining and managing the connected motion between TotalAgility and adjacent pillars (e.g., IVA+ and AP/AR automation) so the portfolio operates as a coherent platform, and so the organization has one visible leader setting direction across that space, not a set of disconnected point products.
Stay ahead of the market. Maintain deep command of the competitive and analyst landscape for IDP and intelligent automation; anticipate market and regulatory shifts — including e-invoicing and compliance mandates — and position the portfolio ahead of them.
Ground decisions in evidence. Lead customer and market discovery; synthesize research, product usage data, and field input into clear, defensible prioritization and investment decisions.
Drive adoption. Own go-to-market strategy for the pillar in partnership with Marketing, Sales, and Channel — positioning, packaging, pricing, and launch — and measure adoption, calibrating quickly where results diverge from plan.
Communicate with altitude. Communicate strategy, roadmap, and trade-offs credibly across every audience, from engineering teams to the executive team, board, customers, and prospects.
Shape inorganic bets. Partner with Corporate Development on build, partner, and acquire decisions that accelerate the IDP and TotalAgility roadmap.
Instrument the business. Establish the metrics and operating cadence that measure progress against strategic and financial goals, and hold the organization accountable to them.

Required Experience

Qualifications

10+ years in enterprise software product management, including senior leadership of a product line or platform at scale, and a track record as a respected leader among mid- to large-enterprise software companies.
Deep, hands-on expertise in Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) — capture, OCR, classification, and extraction — and in Intelligent Automation / BPM platforms such as TotalAgility.
Demonstrated command of applied AI in document and workflow automation: machine learning, GenAI/LLM-based extraction, and emerging agentic automation patterns.
A builder's track record: proven ability not just to set strategy but to ship — owning a roadmap end to end and delivering releases that moved the business.
A demonstrated pattern of staying close to customers and the market personally — this role requires someone who is visible, engaged, and comfortable driving both strategy and execution, not someone who prefers to work in isolation and hand off a finished plan.
Strong commercial fluency: proven ability to own product-level financial targets (bookings, NRR, GRR) and to make disciplined investment trade-offs across a portfolio.
A healthy balance of technical depth, financial rigor, and go-to-market instinct.
Ability to lead, motivate, and hold teams accountable, including influence without authority across a matrixed, cross-functional organization.
Executive presence and outstanding communication — able to articulate complex strategy simply and credibly to boards, executives, customers, and prospects.

At In Tandem, we build technology that helps families manage everyday routines and navigate life's biggest transitions. Through our four brands—OurFamilyWizard, Cozi, FamilyWall, and Custody Navigator—we help families stay organized, communicate well, and foster healthy childhoods.

OurFamilyWizard serves hundreds of thousands of families navigating separation, divorce, and shared custody — and the way families find us is unlike most consumer products. Some arrive on their own. Each path carries different intent, trust, and urgency, and turning that distinctive multi-channel model into lasting customer value is the core of this opportunity.

And with success here, there's real opportunity to shape growth and monetization across the broader In Tandem portfolio.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with real organizational reach. You'll use AI as a real execution lever, moving faster on research, modeling, and experimentation than a traditional growth function could.

A mission-connected operator who connects growth to real-world impact and cares about what happens to the families using OurFamilyWizard.
A hands-on strategist who loves being close to the work—establishing playbooks, building learning foundations, and turning strategy into experiments and results.
Skilled at reading consumer psychology and translating context-specific conditions into strong hypotheses that reduce friction and move parents to the right next action.
A collaborative leader who aligns cross-functional teams around shared priorities without relying on formal authority—and communicates up with the clarity to drive executive alignment.

AI-native: you use current tools to improve the speed and quality of research, modeling, prototyping, and experimentation—while remaining accountable for the output.

In Tandem brings together a growing portfolio of trusted tools that support families—and the professionals who guide them—through the moments that matter most. We bring clarity to chaos and stability to daily family life, helping parents feel less stressed so kids can have healthier childhoods.

Founded in 2009, Superhuman empowers over 40 million people, 50,000 organizations, and 3,000 educational institutions worldwide to eliminate busywork and focus on what matters. Learn more at superhuman.com and about our values here.

The Opportunity

Enterprise email doesn’t get bought the way consumer email gets downloaded. Someone has to believe Mail will change how their team works, make that case to their own leadership, and then get a few hundred people to actually change a habit they’ve had for a decade. That is the job.

Superhuman Mail is the fastest email experience in the world, and it is loved — see what our customers say. Individuals adopt it in minutes. Organizations are harder: the buyer needs proof, the champion needs ammunition, and the team needs a switch that doesn’t cost them a week of feeling slow.

We’re hiring a Product Manager, Admin & Buyer Experience
to own that arc for Mail — from the moment a buyer starts evaluating us through the moment their team is fully switched over. You’ll own Mail’s admin and usage-visibility surfaces, and you’ll own the onboarding experience that determines whether a signed deal becomes a deployed one.

This is a buyer-facing product role, not a compliance-queue role. You’ll spend real time with economic buyers, IT admins, and internal champions, and you’ll work closely with Sales and CS — while holding a clear point of view about which enterprise needs are patterns worth building for and which are one-offs. We want you to focus on what is stopping someone from buying the product, partnering with customers to understand what they need to buy and expand. Our broader platform teams own the cross-suite identity and Super Admin foundation; you own what makes Mail specifically worth buying and easy to roll out on top of it.

In This Role, You Will

Own the product roadmap for Mail’s admin and team-management experience, including usage visibility, activity and adoption reporting, and the audit and access visibility enterprise IT expects.
Own the enterprise onboarding and migration experience — making it effortless for a new team to bring their organization into Mail.
Give champions the tools to make the case internally: clear evidence of who is using Mail, how, and what it’s worth to their organization.
Define and improve the enterprise buyer journey end to end — evaluation, pilot, deployment, expansion, and renewal.
Build a shared, prioritized view of enterprise needs with Sales and CS, distinguishing durable patterns from individual requests, and communicate tradeoffs with clarity and conviction.
Partner with our platform, security, and compliance teams so Mail plugs cleanly into the suite’s identity, provisioning, and governance foundation — without duplicating it.
Measure what matters: activation, early-week retention, and feature adoption for enterprise teams, plus the admin surfaces that prove value to the buyer.
Shape our ICP and define the Product Market Fit journey

Qualifications

You have 4+ years in product management, including experience with admin, account management, onboarding, or usage-analytics products in a B2B SaaS environment.
You have worked directly with enterprise buyers and admins, and you can point to deals or deployments your product work unblocked.
You understand the enterprise IT landscape — SSO, SCIM, RBAC, audit logging, provisioning — well enough to design for it and to partner credibly with security and compliance teams.
You have experience with both self-serve and enterprise motions, and you understand how a product-led funnel behaves inside a large organization.
You have designed for multiple distinct user types at once: IT admins, end users, and the finance or procurement stakeholders who sign.
You have a track record of building simple experiences on top of genuinely complex systems.

Competencies

Enterprise Empathy: You deeply understand IT admins and economic buyers — their workflows, their constraints, and what it takes to earn their trust. You advocate for these often-overlooked users relentlessly.
Commercial Judgment: You can tell a real pattern from a loud escalation. You partner closely with Sales and CS, set expectations honestly, and hold your roadmap without damaging the relationship.
Systems Thinking: You design for scale and consistency across products while preserving the flexibility each product needs. You anticipate edge cases and build systems that hold up under real enterprise complexity.
AI-First Operator: You embed AI into daily workflows, rituals, and decision-making. You model fluency, curiosity, and visible use of AI to raise the bar for speed, quality, and customer impact.
Extreme Ownership: You act as if you are 100% responsible for your own outcomes as well as the outcomes of the company. You do this without stepping on toes.
Results Driven: You work tirelessly in pursuit of your results; you quickly take the initiative and own it when results are off; you course-correct and get scrappy if necessary.
Customer-Centered Innovator: You redesign experiences to create AI-native magic — delighting customers through faster, smarter, and more effective workflows that deliver measurable outcomes.
Low Ego: You put the company ahead of yourself. Most of our discussions are about results and how to amplify success.
Has a demonstrated ability to work independently with minimal guidance, proactively manages tasks and priorities across multiple projects, analyzes and executes work efficiently, collaborates effectively with cross-functional teams, and thrives in fast-paced, results-driven environments.

Summary

Tungsten Automation is the leader in Intelligent Document Processing, and TotalAgility is the platform at the center of that leadership. As enterprises move from document capture to AI-native, agentic automation, we are looking for a Sr. Director of Product Management to own the roadmap and delivery of our Intelligent Document Processing pillar and the TotalAgility platform.

This is a senior, high-ownership role for a product leader who can both set direction and drive it to release. You will define where IDP goes next — AI-native capture, classification and extraction, agentic document workflows, and embedded compliance — and you will be accountable for driving it, allowing oversight and commitment to success through the process. You will turn market signal, competitive pressure, and customer need into a roadmap the organization can execute against, then partner closely with Engineering to bring it to market on time and at quality.

You will be the connective tissue between vision and execution: setting the multi-year strategy for IDP and TotalAgility, sequencing the roadmap against real delivery constraints, and owning the commercial outcomes — bookings, revenue growth, and net revenue retention — that prove it is working. This is a chance to shape how the world's largest enterprises process their most critical documents in the era of agentic AI.

Job Purpose

Own the investment strategy, product vision, roadmap, and end-to-end delivery for the Intelligent Document Processing pillar and the TotalAgility platform — accountable for both the strategic direction and the operational and financial results of the business.

Key Responsibilities

Drive execution end to end. Translate the roadmap into prioritized, well-scoped releases and partner closely with Engineering to ship on schedule, at quality, and with measurable customer impact. This role is accountable for delivery, not just direction.
Own the numbers. Set and own product growth targets in partnership with Finance; be accountable for bookings, revenue growth, net revenue retention (NRR), and gross revenue retention (GRR) in the IDP pillar.
Lead the AI agenda. Own the AI and document-intelligence strategy for the platform — capture, classification, extraction, and agentic document workflows — including build-versus-partner decisions and how AI capabilities are packaged, metered, and priced.
Be the visible face of the product. Stay personally and consistently close to customers and the market — this is a flagship product, and the strategy behind it needs to be shaped in the room with customers, not developed in isolation and handed down. Participate directly in customer meetings, executive briefings, and prospect conversations, and treat that engagement as core to the job, not an occasional add-on.
Own the platform story across the broader portfolio. Drive product strategy and thought leadership not just for TotalAgility, but across the wider DWA portfolio — defining and managing the connected motion between TotalAgility and adjacent pillars (e.g., IVA+ and AP/AR automation) so the portfolio operates as a coherent platform, and so the organization has one visible leader setting direction across that space, not a set of disconnected point products.
Stay ahead of the market. Maintain deep command of the competitive and analyst landscape for IDP and intelligent automation; anticipate market and regulatory shifts — including e-invoicing and compliance mandates — and position the portfolio ahead of them.
Ground decisions in evidence. Lead customer and market discovery; synthesize research, product usage data, and field input into clear, defensible prioritization and investment decisions.
Drive adoption. Own go-to-market strategy for the pillar in partnership with Marketing, Sales, and Channel — positioning, packaging, pricing, and launch — and measure adoption, calibrating quickly where results diverge from plan.
Communicate with altitude. Communicate strategy, roadmap, and trade-offs credibly across every audience, from engineering teams to the executive team, board, customers, and prospects.
Shape inorganic bets. Partner with Corporate Development on build, partner, and acquire decisions that accelerate the IDP and TotalAgility roadmap.
Instrument the business. Establish the metrics and operating cadence that measure progress against strategic and financial goals, and hold the organization accountable to them.

While this job description describes what is anticipated as the requirements of the position, the requirements are subject to change based upon any changing needs and requirements of the business.

Required Experience

Qualifications

10+ years in enterprise software product management, including senior leadership of a product line or platform at scale, and a track record as a respected leader among mid- to large-enterprise software companies.
Deep, hands-on expertise in Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) — capture, OCR, classification, and extraction — and in Intelligent Automation / BPM platforms such as TotalAgility.
Demonstrated command of applied AI in document and workflow automation: machine learning, GenAI/LLM-based extraction, and emerging agentic automation patterns.
A builder's track record: proven ability not just to set strategy but to ship — owning a roadmap end to end and delivering releases that moved the business.
A demonstrated pattern of staying close to customers and the market personally — this role requires someone who is visible, engaged, and comfortable driving both strategy and execution, not someone who prefers to work in isolation and hand off a finished plan.
Strong commercial fluency: proven ability to own product-level financial targets (bookings, NRR, GRR) and to make disciplined investment trade-offs across a portfolio.
A healthy balance of technical depth, financial rigor, and go-to-market instinct.
Ability to lead, motivate, and hold teams accountable, including influence without authority across a matrixed, cross-functional organization.
Executive presence and outstanding communication — able to articulate complex strategy simply and credibly to boards, executives, customers, and prospects.
Sharp problem-solving, sound independent judgment, and decisive decision-making under ambiguity.
Experience in compliance-driven or regulated document domains (e.g., e-invoicing mandates, regulated financial or public-sector workflows) is a strong plus.

Key Performance Indicators

Bookings and revenue growth; net revenue retention; gross revenue retention; on-time roadmap delivery; product adoption and usage; and competitive win rate for the IDP pillar. .
